name: Lungwort
grown_as: A hardy perennial for shade by the pond, flowering in early spring.
habit: A low clump: short upright flowering stems 20 to 30 cm in early spring, then a mound of large spotted leaves 30 to 45 cm across through the summer.

leaf.arrangement: Large leaves from the base; smaller alternate leaves on the flowering stems
leaf.outline: Basal leaves oval to heart-shaped, 7 to 15 cm long; stem leaves smaller and oval
leaf.base: Basal leaves abruptly rounded to heart-shaped where they meet the stalk; stem leaves stalkless and half-clasping
leaf.veins: A midrib and a few side veins, not deeply pressed in
leaf.surface: Rough with short bristly hairs; scattered with pale green to whitish spots
leaf.stalk: Basal leaves on long stalks, about as long as the blade; stem leaves none
leaf.colour: Mid to dark green with pale spots

flower.form: A small funnel: a narrow tube opening to five rounded lobes
flower.petals: Five, joined into the tube, the lobes spreading
flower.colour: Pink when they open, turning violet then blue as they age, so pink and blue flowers sit together on one plant
flower.centre: A small throat with tufts of hairs, stamens hidden
flower.behind: A tubular, five-angled, hairy green calyx about half the length of the tube
flower.carried: In loose clusters at the tops of short leafy stems, the flowers nodding to facing out

fruit: Small nutlets inside the calyx; not usually noticed.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from bought plants or division
winter: In mild winters a few spotted leaves remain; otherwise only the crown with the new flower shoots appearing in late winter.

leaf: oval leaf with an abruptly rounded or heart-shaped base on a long stalk
pale spots scattered over the surface
bloom: small funnel-shaped flowers with five lobes
pink and blue flowers in the same cluster
young: a clump of large spotted leaves on long stalks
flower: short leafy stems with clusters of pink and blue flowers
dormant: a few spotted leaves or just the crown at the soil
new flower shoots in late winter

look_alikes: Other lungworts: narrow-leaved lungwort (Pulmonaria longifolia) has long narrow leaves; Pulmonaria saccharata has larger, more heavily silvered leaves. Comfrey is much larger and unspotted. Green alkanet has unspotted leaves and pure blue flowers with a white eye.
